seoDescription: Hurt in a car crash in Taylor? Taylor had 1,916 crashes and 12 deaths in 2024, and Telegraph at Eureka was fifth in Wayne County. Covers who pays your bills under no-fault, what to do when the other driver is uninsured or from out of state, how fault is decided, who owns Telegraph, Eureka, and the subdivision streets, and the one-year and three-year deadlines. Free review. (313) 406-7606.

Eureka at Telegraph had 36 injuries in 2024. That ties it with 7 Mile at I-75 in Detroit for the most injuries of any intersection on Wayne County’s top-ten list.

Telegraph is a multi-lane road through the city, from Van Born at the north end to the Brownstown line at the south. Its signals at Eureka, Goddard, Northline, Ecorse, and Van Born carry heavy left-turn traffic into the shopping centers and apartment complexes. The crashes are:

items.v: left turns across several lanes of oncoming traffic
red-light crashes
rear-end crashes in the stacked turn lanes
drivers pulling out of driveways between signals
pedestrians crossing between bus stops and complexes

c.v: Fault at a Telegraph left turn is governed by the duty to yield to oncoming traffic (MCL 257.650). Telegraph belongs to MDOT.
Eureka Road and the Southland corridor.
Eureka runs east from Telegraph past Southland Center, the big-box stores, and the restaurants, to Pardee, Allen, and the I-75 interchange. The typical crashes involve:

items.v: driveways and parking-lot exits
rear-end crashes in stop-and-go traffic
lane changes into an occupied lane (MCL 257.642(1)(a))
pedestrians in the lots and crossing Eureka between stores

Whose road it is: the State, the county, or the City.
Taylor is a city, and it owns its subdivision streets. The main roads belong to two other agencies:

items.v: MDOT: Telegraph, I-75, and I-94. A road-defect claim against MDOT goes to the Court of Claims, with written notice filed there within 120 days (MCL 691.1404). (Champine, Mich 2022.)
Wayne County: Eureka, Allen, and other mile roads, through its Department of Public Services. A claim against the county takes written notice within 120 days (MCL 691.1402, 691.1404).

sections.heading: Who pays after a Taylor crash

c.v: Your own auto insurer pays these benefits regardless of fault (MCL 500.3107):

items.v: your medical expenses, up to the PIP level you chose
85 percent of lost wages for up to three years, up to the monthly cap DIFS sets each year
replacement services at $20 a day
attendant care

c.v: If you have no policy, a resident relative’s policy pays (MCL 500.3114). If none exists, an occupant claims from the insurer of the vehicle they were in (MCL 500.3114(4)), and then the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan (MCL 500.3172), capped at $250,000 for medical benefits. A pedestrian or cyclist hit by a car, with no household policy, claims through the Assigned Claims Plan (MCL 500.3115).

The insurer must receive written notice within one year (MCL 500.3145(1)). It must pay each bill within 30 days of reasonable proof, or owe 12 percent interest (MCL 500.3142). Since the 2019 reform, PIP medical coverage is no longer unlimited unless you chose it, so the level on your declarations page matters. See our

A person who owned a car and was required to insure it, but did not, is generally barred from PIP benefits for their own injuries (MCL 500.3113(b)). A driver who was operating their own uninsured vehicle cannot recover pain-and-suffering damages, whoever was at fault (MCL 500.3135(2)(c)). A passenger or pedestrian with no policy of their own is not barred, and the Assigned Claims Plan may be the payer.
Taylor sits next to the airport, so rental cars and out-of-state drivers are part of the traffic on Telegraph and I-94. If one of them hits you, two separate questions arise:

items.v: your own Michigan no-fault benefits are paid as usual.
this can involve the rental company’s coverage, the driver’s home-state policy, and the out-of-state insurer’s certification to provide Michigan coverage (MCL 500.3163).

c.v: A non-resident generally has no Michigan PIP claim of their own unless they own a vehicle registered and insured in Michigan (MCL 500.3113(c)).
Your claim against the at-fault driver.

For pain and suffering, you need a threshold injury: death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement (MCL 500.3135(1)). A serious impairment is an objectively manifested impairment of an important body function that affects your general ability to lead your normal life. It does not have to be permanent (MCL 500.3135(5);

You can also recover lost wages beyond the three years or above the monthly cap, and medical bills above your chosen PIP level (MCL 500.3135(3)(c)). The suit must be filed within three years (MCL 600.5805(2)). The mini tort claim recovers up to $3,000 in vehicle damage not covered by your policy (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)). If the at-fault driver’s insurer will not pay it, the claim is filed in the 23rd District Court.

Wayne County recorded 1,331 alcohol-involved crashes in 2024. A crash caused by a drunk driver leaving a bar or restaurant on Telegraph or Eureka can add a claim against the business, if it served a visibly intoxicated person or a minor. That claim has its own rules (MCL 436.1801(3), (4)):

items.v: Written notice must go to the business within 120 days after you hire a lawyer.
The drunk driver must be named and kept in the suit.
The suit must be filed within two years, not three.

sections.heading: What to do after a Taylor crash

c.v: Call 911 and get the police report.

items.v: Michigan requires a report for any crash with injury or $1,000 in damage (MCL 257.622). Crashes in the city are worked by the Taylor Police Department, and freeway crashes may be worked by the Michigan State Police.

Get the vehicles, the plates, the other driver’s license and insurance card, the signals, and the lane markings. If the other driver shows an out-of-state or rental-car document, photograph that too. Note every business with a camera facing the scene, because footage is kept for days, not weeks.

c.v: Get medical care the same day.

faqs.question: How many crashes are there in Taylor?

answer.v: The State Police recorded 1,916 crashes in Taylor in 2024. They killed 12 people and injured 547, 26 of them seriously. Eureka at Telegraph had 68 crashes and 36 injuries, the fifth-highest crash count of any intersection in Wayne County.

faqs.question: The driver who hit me on Telegraph had no insurance. What now?

answer.v: Your own no-fault insurer, a household member’s insurer, or the Assigned Claims Plan pays your medical bills and lost wages regardless of fault. Your pain-and-suffering claim depends on whether you carry uninsured motorist coverage. Without it, the claim is worth what the uninsured driver can personally pay. Check your declarations page today.

faqs.question: I was hit by an out-of-state driver in a rental car. Who pays?

answer.v: Your own no-fault insurer pays your benefits as usual. Your claim against the driver can involve the rental company’s coverage, the driver’s home policy, and that insurer’s Michigan certification. The order depends on the rental agreement and the policies.

faqs.question: I was hit while walking on Eureka or Telegraph. Who pays my medical bills?

answer.v: Your own household’s auto policy pays if you have one. If not, the Assigned Claims Plan pays. (MCL 500.3115.) A pedestrian has the same pain-and-suffering claim as a driver, subject to the threshold.

faqs.question: Where would my Taylor case be filed?

answer.v: Mini tort claims and claims up to $25,000 go to the 23rd District Court on Goddard Road. Injury suits over $25,000 go to the Third Judicial Circuit Court in Detroit.
